response: In simple terms, gravity is the invisible force that pulls objects with mass toward each other. The more mass an object has, the stronger its pull. That’s why Earth, which is huge, keeps us grounded and makes things fall. It also keeps the Moon orbiting around us and the planets circling the Sun. Even light is affected by gravity, bending around massive objects like black holes. This universal attraction shapes the structure of the entire cosmos, from the way galaxies cluster together to the path of a thrown ball. That is gravity.
